evidence: DESIGN.md named `promptctl/tmux-control-mode-js/SPEC.md` as protocol authority with no link or indication it is external; 4498ed8 turned it into a GitHub URL.
guidance_note: When a design doc cites an external document as authority, link every external document it cites (SPEC and IMPL alike) in the first draft.

evidence: The phoenix-daemon bullet listed four responsibilities joined by 'and' directly above the claim that each crate's purpose is one conjunction-free sentence; the fix rewrote both daemon and cli bullets.
guidance_note: Before asserting a property of every item in a list, check each item in that list against it.

evidence: The spec said `close()` 'drops the transport locally and sends nothing' with no mention of reaping; the agent noted the code already reaps but the spec the reconnect loop relies on was silent, and fixed the text.

The diagram showed phoenix-cli depending only on phoenix-daemon while milestones built save/list from capture+store directly; the agent confirmed the real manifests disagreed with the diagram and redrew it from Cargo.toml.
guidance_note: Derive dependency diagrams from the actual manifests rather than drawing them from intent.

evidence: The duplicated block sits between `<!-- BEGIN LIT INTEGRATION -->` markers that `lit init` writes into both files; the generator is the single source and hand-deduplication would be overwritten.

4498ed8 strengthened 'neither depending on phoenix' to 'depend on nothing', which made §3.1's tmux-control `Layout` read as phoenix-core's field type; phoenix-core actually has its own `Layout`, so the doc was ambiguous rather than wrong, and 246b1ba added a clarifying line.
guidance_note: When a fix tightens a claim (e.g. 'depends on nothing'), re-read every other section that mentions the same types for text the stronger claim now appears to contradict.

evidence: F1's fix linked SPEC.md but left 'IMPL §2.1/§2.2/§2.4' citations to a never-introduced document from the same repo; 246b1ba added the IMPL.md link.
guidance_note: When fixing one unresolvable citation, grep the doc for every other citation prefix (SPEC §, IMPL §) and resolve them in the same commit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 4498ed8 did not touch §3.4, and the 'no process spawns' vs §5 'one ps pass' contradiction was in the original draft; 246b1ba reworded to 'no tmux process spawns'.
guidance_note: When a summary paragraph makes an absolute claim ('no process spawns'), check it against every section describing the same operation.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 4498ed8 did not touch §7; 'single writer' with no enforcement was original text, and the agent confirmed in code that `free_generation_id` races, documented the lock and filed tmux-store-9le.
guidance_note: When a design doc asserts an invariant like 'single writer', name the mechanism that enforces it in the same sentence.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 246b1ba only added the Layout-ownership line to §4, while `sessions: NonEmpty<Session>` was original; the doc indeed did not say what happens at zero sessions, but the agent's live check showed `list-panes -a` returns `%error` there, so the type is fine and documenting a capture failure is the right fix.
guidance_note: When a type encodes a non-empty invariant, state in the doc which layer enforces it for each level (tmux for windows/panes, capture for sessions).

narrative: A design-doc PR reviewed four times. Round 0 found five real doc gaps plus a generated-block duplication the agent correctly declined. Round 1 had two fix-caused findings (IMPL left unlinked after SPEC was linked; a tightened 'depend on nothing' claim reading as contradicted by §3.1) alongside two pre-existing contradictions, so the round would have happened regardless. Round 2's zero-session finding was pre-existing and the agent verified tmux behavior live before settling the text.
guidance_observations: The agent checked doc claims against the real manifests and code before fixing, which turned two doc findings into filed code bugs (tmux-store-9le, tmux-capture-wxo).
The agent corrected its own plan reply after a live tmux check instead of letting a wrong premise stand on the thread.

evidence: The buffer holds one partial line from a child the crate spawned and owns, so unbounded growth needs tmux itself to misbehave and the pushback stands; but a cap that raises a loud overflow error would not be a silent failure, so the no-silent-failure citation argues against a version nobody proposed.
The hunk shows `value as u8` after a loop that rejects only digits > 7, so `\777` truncates to 255; b20cf2e uses `u8::try_from` and adds a test.
guidance_note: When narrowing an accumulated integer, use a checked conversion rather than `as` from the start.

evidence: The hunk shows `send` failure setting `self.closed = true` and `read` short-circuiting on it, so buffered stdout becomes unreachable; b20cf2e replaced the flag with typed `Open|Closed` state, a structural fix rather than a second flag.
guidance_note: Ship a regression test with any state restructure that exists to enable a specific scenario (here: read after failed send).

evidence: `Stdio::null()` hid tmux startup errors that never reach `%error` framing; the agent chose `Stdio::inherit()` over piping stderr because an undrained second pipe can deadlock the child, which is a sound reason.
guidance_note: Do not discard a child's stderr unless every failure mode is known to arrive on another channel.

evidence: decode.rs decoded malformed escapes to `?` and its own module doc noted DESIGN.md disagreed; the agent fixed DESIGN.md and deleted the explanatory paragraph.
guidance_note: When code knowingly diverges from the design doc, update the doc in the same PR instead of writing a comment explaining the divergence.

evidence: The code and tests type `SubscriptionChanged.session` as `Option<SessionId>` per SPEC §7.9 while the DESIGN.md sketch had it required; the sketch was corrected.
guidance_note: When an implementation changes a type sketched in the design doc, update the sketch in the same PR.

evidence: The hunk shows `Ok(0)` latching `closed`, which per `std::io::Read` also happens for an empty buffer; the typed state passes reads straight through so nothing latches, and the trait doc now qualifies `Ok(0)`.
guidance_note: Ship the test for the scenario a restructure claims to fix (an empty-buffer read) in the same commit.

evidence: Rust std's unix `Child::kill` returns Ok without signalling once `wait` has recorded a status, so the second `reap()` in `Drop` could not hit a recycled PID; the agent cited that source and the typed-state rewrite reaps once by construction anyway.
The live tests looped on a blocking `read()` with no deadline, so a stalled tmux would hang `cargo test`; b20cf2e added a threaded `read_through_end` with a 10s `recv_timeout`.
guidance_note: When adding a deadline to one blocking test helper, apply it to every read helper in the suite (here `read_available` too) and make the reader thread report its own failure through the channel.

evidence: The hunk shows a non-`%` line outside a block silently returned, against DESIGN.md's 'surfaced as Unknown, never dropped'; the early return was deleted and tests updated.
guidance_note: When removing a special case, add a test for the exact input the special case carved out (the empty line).

evidence: Rust's integer `parse` accepts a leading `+`, contradicting the doc comment's 'strict' claim; one digits-only `parse_decimal` replaced the three parsers.
guidance_note: When a parser claims strictness, write a test for each input the standard library accepts that the claim excludes (a leading sign).

evidence: `parse_prefixed` inlined `from_utf8(...).parse()` instead of calling the fields parser, duplicating the `+` leniency; it now calls `fields::parse_decimal`.
guidance_note: Route every numeric field through the one shared parser from the first draft.

evidence: F3's typed-state restructure existed to keep stdout readable after a failed send, but b20cf2e shipped no test for that scenario; fd67a3e added `failed_send_leaves_buffered_output_readable`.
guidance_note: When a fix exists to enable a specific scenario, ship the test for that scenario in the fix commit.

evidence: The finding targets F9's new threaded helper; the agent showed that the timeout panic drops `IsolatedTmux`, whose `kill-session` makes the client exit, so the blocked read gets EOF and the transport is reaped, and confirmed this against a live tmux.
guidance_note: When adding a helper whose cleanup depends on drop order, document the teardown path in its doc comment as you write it.

evidence: F7's fix promised a zero-length read latches nothing but added no test; fd67a3e added `empty_buffer_read_leaves_the_transport_readable`.
guidance_note: When a fix exists to enable a specific scenario, ship the test for that scenario in the fix commit.

evidence: This duplicates F13 from another sweep: the read-after-failed-send scenario F3's fix enabled had no test; resolved by the same fd67a3e test.
guidance_note: When a fix exists to enable a specific scenario, ship the test for that scenario in the fix commit.

evidence: Same claim as F14 on F9's new helper; it calls teardown an 'unrelated race', but `IsolatedTmux` dropping during unwind is the deterministic path, which the agent checked live. The claim does hold for the non-tmux callers that F22's fix later added (see F26).
guidance_note: When adding a helper whose cleanup depends on drop order, document the teardown path in its doc comment as you write it.

evidence: F11/F12's fix made `parse_decimal` reject a leading sign but added no test for it; fd67a3e added `signed_numeric_fields_do_not_parse`.
guidance_note: When a fix rejects a new input shape, add a test feeding that exact shape in the fix commit.

evidence: F10's fix generalized the non-`%` case to Unknown but tested only a non-empty garbage line, not the empty line the old early return was about; fd67a3e added `empty_line_outside_block_is_unknown`.
guidance_note: When removing a special case, add a test for the exact input the special case carved out.

evidence: F9's fix moved the `assert!(n > 0, ...)` into a detached thread, so its message became a generic channel-disconnected error instead of the test failure; fd67a3e sends a `Result` through the channel.
guidance_note: When moving assertions onto a worker thread, send the failure reason back through the channel instead of panicking in the thread.

evidence: `terminate_line` was original code and let an embedded newline split one send into two tmux commands. The first fix (3a1535d) rejected any newline, which the agent later reversed because valid tmux state (cwds, option values) contains newlines. The final fix (6cdd6d2) ports tmux's `args_escape` into a `CommandLine` type.
guidance_note: Before rejecting an input character, check whether legitimate domain values contain it, and prefer escaping at the type boundary.

evidence: F9's fix bounded only the live-tmux read helper, leaving `read_available`'s unbounded blocking loop; 6cdd6d2 routed both through one `read_until` with the 10s timeout.
guidance_note: When adding a deadline to one blocking test helper, sweep the file for every other blocking read loop.

evidence: The original live-test loops already matched only `%end `; F9's fix moved that check into `read_through_end` unchanged, so this is relocated pre-review logic, not fix-caused. The reply-hint says pushback but the reply says 'Valid, and fixed in 6cdd6d2'.
guidance_note: When detecting protocol terminators in tests, reuse the codec's own terminator logic instead of a byte scan.

evidence: F23's fix added `closes_a_block`, a prefix scan that requires a trailing space and so misses a bare `%end` the codec force-closes; 7ccf638 drives the bytes through the real `Codec`.
guidance_note: When a fix needs a rule the crate already owns (which line closes a block), call the crate's implementation instead of writing a second one.

evidence: The hostile-argument test added with F21's CommandLine fix (6cdd6d2) removed its temp file only at the end, so a failed assertion leaks it; 7ccf638 added an RAII guard, and the agent found and fixed the socket leak in `IsolatedTmux` too.
guidance_note: Give every temp resource a test creates a Drop guard, matching the existing harness pattern.

evidence: The flagged commit ac8dd6e (socket removal) is unrelated. The real cause is F22's fix in 6cdd6d2, which routed `read_available`'s `sh -c cat` callers through the threaded helper, whose teardown story holds only for live-tmux callers. The agent corrected the comment and filed tmux-testing-h1t rather than widening the production API on the last round.
guidance_note: When extending a helper to new callers, re-check that its doc comment's guarantees hold for each new caller.

narrative: Round 0's twelve findings were mostly real and well fixed, often structurally (typed transport state). Every round-1 finding traced to a round-0 fix: five missing tests for scenarios the fixes existed to enable, a diagnostic regression from moving asserts onto a thread, and two wrong-premise leak claims about the new helper. The newline-injection finding (F21) got a first fix that rejected valid state, which the agent reversed into an escaping `CommandLine` type. Rounds 4 and 6 again found only fix-caused issues in the test helpers. Rounds 5 and 7 were round-cap non-reviews.
guidance_observations: Fix commits repeatedly shipped without the regression test for the scenario they existed to fix, which cost a whole review round of test-coverage findings.
Test-helper fixes were applied to one helper at a time (deadline, terminator detection, teardown), so each later round found the same gap in a sibling helper.
The agent verified pushbacks empirically (std source for kill-after-wait, a live tmux for the teardown path) rather than arguing from assumption.

evidence: The hunk shows `(0..s.len()).find_map(...)` restarting at every byte, so a rejected overflowing digit run is retried at an interior offset; the agent reproduced it (start=2 gives 999999999) and replaced byte-offset scanning with maximal-token splitting rather than an overflow guard.
guidance_note: When scanning text for a token, iterate over maximal tokens rather than byte offsets so a rejected token can never be re-entered from inside.

narrative: One real finding about version parsing resuming inside a rejected digit run. The agent reproduced it, then fixed the cause (byte-offset scan) instead of the symptom (overflow), with less code and tests for both overflow directions. The second round approved.
guidance_observations: Reproducing the finding before deciding, then fixing the scan shape rather than adding a guard, closed the PR in one fix round.

evidence: The packet shows only client.rs's MockTransport, not the copies in connection_state.rs and notifications.rs, so the claimed triplication and drift cannot be checked. The PR was closed as superseded by #5 with an identical branch, and how this finding fared there is not in the packet.
guidance_note: When test files in one PR need the same fake, put it in the shared `tests/support` module the PR already creates.

evidence: The file header in F1's hunk says `Client::connect`'s greeting consumption is covered in connection_state.rs, so an inline comment calling the handshake unbuilt ticket `.4` work is stale. The PR was closed as superseded by #5, and the fate of the finding is not in the packet.
guidance_note: When a slice lands the work an earlier comment deferred, grep for comments that name that ticket and update them.

evidence: The MockTransport in the hunk has a `fail_next_send` hook and no read-failure counterpart, so the `TmuxError::Read` branch with its Closed transition plausibly goes untested. The PR was closed as superseded by #5.
guidance_note: When a fake transport gets a failure hook for one direction, add the matching hook for the other direction and test both error branches.

evidence: The hunk cuts off right after `detach()` calls `send`, so whether a send error leaves the state at `Ready` cannot be seen. The doc calls detach best-effort and not gated on state, which does not settle whether a failure should close it. The PR was closed as superseded by #5.
guidance_note: When several paths touch the transport, route their failure-to-Closed transition through one helper so no path can skip it.

evidence: The hunk shows `execute` setting `ConnectionState::Closed` on send, read, or EOF failure without calling `transport.close()`, so the exited child stays unreaped until the Client drops. `SpawnTransport`'s Drop does reap, so 'leak' overstates it to a zombie that lives as long as the Client. The PR was closed as superseded by #5.
guidance_note: Make the transition to Closed a single method that both sets the state and closes the transport, so the state cannot claim teardown that did not happen.

narrative: One review round with five findings, none answered. The agent closed the PR because its base branch was deleted when #3 merged, and opened #5 with the identical branch. The packet does not show whether these findings were addressed in #5.
guidance_observations: Stacking a PR on a slice branch that GitHub deletes on merge orphaned a reviewed PR and its unanswered threads; retargeting the PR's base before merging the parent avoids it.
